headline: Highest risk is B data leakage: RD-Agent’s broad network/API egress can expose shared inputs, while the prompt-engineering repo offers no isolation or runtime controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a static prompt-engineering repository with no runnable I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest B’s outputs. B can browse and process external content, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel or parser bridge. The only plausible pathway is manual copy/paste or external orchestration, which keeps blast radius small.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies B-generated text into A-derived prompts, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the two, A can become a prompt-injection sink.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected; avoid copy/paste bridges.
Use a provenance label on any text moved from B to A.
Restrict B browsing to trusted domains.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization before any shared handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B touches financial reports, datasets, logs, and secrets and has broad network egress plus API calls, so it can exfiltrate sensitive material if fed shared inputs. A is a docs-only repo with no runtime isolation or data controls, so it does not reduce that risk. The pairwise leakage path exists in default B behavior once sensitive data enters the workflow.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed into B’s workspace, B can transmit them to external APIs.
IF A-derived prompts include confidential text, B may retain it in logs or outputs.
mitigations: Do not place secrets or regulated data in B’s input set.
Rotate API keys before testing the pair.
Disable or proxy B egress for sensitive runs.
Review B logs after each run and delete sensitive artifacts.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data classification filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no declared write or network capabilities, while B supports multiple instances and broad egress. There is no documented shared mutable resource, so direct write-write conflict is not evidenced. Uncertainty remains because A’s empty capability surface does not prove absence of external orchestration, so the safer low rating is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, file conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator gives A hidden write access, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Run only one B instance per workspace.
Lock shared files before writes.
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency checks for shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is a research automation agent that can browse and act on outputs, while A is a prompt-engineering content source that may be treated as authoritative guidance. If B consumes A’s material without verification, errors can cascade into downstream research artifacts or API-driven actions. The pathway is plausible in default workflows, though not directly documented as a hardwired chain.
conditions: IF B ingests A-produced guidance as authoritative, unverified claims can propagate.
IF B uses A-derived prompts to generate reports or API calls, mistakes can cascade.
mitigations: Require human review of A-derived inputs before B uses them.
Add a verification step for citations and facts.
Limit B to draft-only mode for A-sourced content.
Tag A content as non-authoritative in the workflow.
requires-engineering: implement source-trust scoring.

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly handles financial reports, logs, and secrets and sends data to third-party APIs; A is a docs-only repository with no data residency controls. The pair therefore creates a compliance mismatch risk when regulated or confidential data from B’s domain is routed through external services. A is not cited as a data processor because it has no touched data classes.
conditions: IF EU personal data or regulated financial data is processed by B through external APIs, residency or retention obligations may be breached.
IF secrets are stored in B logs, retention policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B runs.
Confirm API-region settings before execution.
Purge B logs after each run.
Document retention and deletion expectations.
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing and retention enforcement.
